head: 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e
notes: Pin held at 1f725ce without checkout; base is an ancestor; overlay applied. Many style hits in this chunk are already in known.json (policy.go NIT-56/66/67/9-r2/2-r2/3-r2/4-r2/11-r2, configserver peekID/startPeek NIT-91..103/106/179/180, registry NIT-51/52/74/75/76/162/7-r2/15-r2, sessions NIT-47/48/49/80/156, routines NIT-13-r2/14-r2/55/61/82/83/85/160/163, shell NIT-44, config NIT-70/154/71/5-r2/72, evals NIT-77/78/155/164/8-r2, dist NIT-58, git NIT-46/64/6-r2, policy_test NIT-68/158/12-r2) and were not re-reported. Legacy patterns judged out of scope per go.md ENFORCEMENT: lowercase error messages in internal/acdsl (edit.go/rule.go precedent), by-value struct params in internal/acdsl, xErr shadow-dodging names, Re-suffixed regexp vars, bare log.Fatal(err) in configserver main. Cross-chunk suspicions for the station (not chased): (1) cmd/acdsl/main.go:127-137 prepends CheckPolicy diagnostics even when -rule narrows the gated set, so a generation dry-run (-rule X) can go red on unrelated policy violations — correctness lane; (2) com.smine.configserver.plist.template:16 relies on install.sh substituting __PEEK_HOME_ARGS__ (glued after </string>) — verify in the install.sh chunk; (3) peek.SessionsById leaves Session.GitBranch empty (NIT-2) — if an internal/server caller of SessionsById starts reading GitBranch it gets "".

findings.claim: The new per-install constants are re-spelled instead of shared: config.DefaultPeekControlPort = "42442" (installenv.go:9) duplicates the peek-control-port flag default 42442 in cmd/configserver/main.go:52, and the install.env filename owned by config.installEnvPath (installenv.go:11) is re-spelled as the literal "install.env" in the new writeInstallEnv (cmd/configserver/install_windows.go:145).
findings.evidence: Re-read installenv.go:8-12, main.go:52 and install_windows.go:139-149 at 1f725ce; git grep over *.go shows 42442 only at main.go:52 and installenv.go:9 (plus test fixtures), and "install.env" as a production literal only at installenv.go:11 and install_windows.go:145. Changing the default control port in the flag (or the env filename in one package) leaves ExpandInstallMarkers expanding {{PEEK_CONTROL_PORT}} to the old value / reading a file the Windows installer no longer writes. No current divergence, so debt/eventually.
findings.fix: Export one constant for the filename (e.g. config.InstallEnvName) and use it in writeInstallEnv; make the flag default derive from one int constant (e.g. config.DefaultPeekControlPort as int, formatted with strconv.Itoa in installEnvValues).

findings.claim: The listItem-to-Session mapping is written out twice (SessionIndex at peek.go:109-116 and SessionsById at peek.go:144-150), and this change already let the copies drift: the new GitBranch field is populated only in SessionIndex, so SessionsById returns Sessions with GitBranch always empty.
findings.evidence: Re-read peek.go:92-153 at 1f725ce: SessionIndex's literal sets GitBranch: item.Meta.GitBranch, SessionsById's literal does not. git grep shows SessionsById callers only in internal/server/welcome.go:190/383 and no .GitBranch read there, so nothing consumes the gap today — debt/eventually.
findings.fix: Extract one sessionFromItem(item listItem) Session helper (Cwd cleaned, GitBranch, LastActive, Live, Title) and call it from both SessionIndex and SessionsById.

findings.claim: installEnvValues parses install.env into a map[string]string although the file has a fixed, known key set (CONFIGSERVER_PORT, PEEK_PORT, PEEK_CONTROL_PORT as written by writeInstallEnv) and the only consumer reads one key by string literal; RULE-GOLANG-TYPE-001 forbids map[string]string where a typed model can be declared.
findings.evidence: Re-read installenv.go:18-40 and install_windows.go:144 at 1f725ce: ExpandInstallMarkers reads values["PEEK_CONTROL_PORT"] only; every other parsed key is stored and discarded, and a typo in the lookup key would silently yield "" (no compile-time check).
findings.fix: Declare type installEnv struct{ PeekControlPort string } (defaulted to DefaultPeekControlPort) and have installEnvValues fill its field from the PEEK_CONTROL_PORT line; ExpandInstallMarkers reads env.PeekControlPort.
